title: AAP disciplinary derivative integrity and schema-version controls
summary: Year-by-year comparison of restricted fiscal disciplinary registers to their AAP-sorted derivatives shows that some AAP copies are exact reorderings, while others omit/add rows, change EEO/job-group classifications, alter protected-field values, or insert hard-coded subtotal rows. AAP copies therefore must be treated as derived/reporting artifacts with their own version/provenance rather than authoritative duplicates.

claims.claim: The 2013-2014 AAP-sorted file is an exact multiset match to all 53 fiscal-register events across the retained department/name/title/EEO/gender/race/type/reason/date fields, differing only in ordering.

evidence.note: Employee identities remain restricted; comparison result is aggregate only.

claims.claim: The 2014-2015 AAP derivative contains 71 detail rows versus 73 fiscal events, omitting two source events; among matched records it changes EEO classification on 59 rows, including 58 transitions from category 7 to category 9 and one from category 5 to category 9.

The 2015-2016 AAP derivative preserves 123 detail rows plus 12 hard-coded subtotal rows; comparison finds one source-name occurrence missing and one extra, plus a small number of EEO/race/veteran field discrepancies.

evidence.note: Protected-field discrepancy counts are retained without the underlying values.

claims.claim: Two materially different 2016-2017 AAP derivatives exist. The date-retaining variant has 127 detail rows and systematically recodes EEO classifications on 99 rows, including 96 category-7 to category-9 transitions; the subtotal variant also has 127 detail rows plus 12 hard-coded subtotal rows and differs from the fiscal register in only a small number of demographic/department/EEO fields.

evidence.note: This establishes distinct transformations; it does not determine which version was final/official.

claims.claim: The 2017-2018 derivative preserves all 96 detail-event occurrences plus eight subtotal rows but has three event-level field discrepancies; 2018-2019 preserves all 85 detail occurrences plus seven subtotal rows with one IWD discrepancy.

The 2019-2020 derivative has 94 detail rows versus 95 fiscal events, with two fiscal name-occurrences missing and one extra; the 2020-2021 derivative has 55 detail rows versus 54 fiscal events, adding one extra occurrence.

The 2021-2022 AAP derivative is a complete 44-event occurrence match on retained fields plus six subtotal rows; the 2022-2023 derivative preserves all 47 name occurrences plus seven subtotal rows with one veteran-field discrepancy.

No formulas were detected in any of the 29 supplied disciplinary/AAP/verbal-warning workbooks after deterministic conversion; observed AAP subtotal/count rows are hard-coded values rather than formula-derived calculations.

Because AAP derivatives can alter classification values and event population, the fiscal/source register and AAP derivative must each retain their own hash, schema version, transformation provenance and reconciliation report; a filename containing 'sorted' is insufficient evidence of equivalence.

Because fiscal registers from 2016-2017 onward include vehicle Incident rows alongside discipline, an AAP derivative that simply carries the full source population may include non-disciplinary vehicle incidents. AAP analysis must define whether such incidents belong in the disciplinary population rather than assuming every source row represents corrective action.

trigger: Historical disciplinary data is imported, reconciled or transformed for AAP/EEO analysis.
prerequisites: Identify source fiscal register and derivative version by hash.
steps: Parse the source register with a year/schema-specific adapter.
Compare derivative detail rows to the source as a multiset using only the fields retained by that derivative.
Record missing/extra occurrences and changed fields without silently overwriting source values.
Preserve the derivative's transformation/version separately from the authoritative source register.
Require review of unexplained classification/population changes before AAP analysis.
decisions: Whether a derivative is an exact reordering, intentional recoding, incomplete subset, augmented copy or unexplained divergent version.
Which source/version is authoritative for each field and reporting period.
controls: Never treat sorted/AAP workbooks as byte- or record-equivalent copies without reconciliation.
Subtotal rows must never be ingested as employee/event rows.
Hard-coded subtotal counts should be recalculated from validated detail rows rather than trusted blindly.
Protected-field discrepancies require controlled review without exposing values in generalized knowledge.
Define and test the reporting population explicitly; do not count vehicle Incident rows as discipline unless the governing AAP methodology requires it.
unresolved_questions: What documented AAP/EEO methodology explains the systematic category-7 to category-9 recoding in the 2014-2015 and one 2016-2017 derivative?
Which 2016-2017 AAP derivative was the final/official reporting input?
What explains the missing/extra event occurrences in 2014-2015, 2015-2016, 2019-2020 and 2020-2021 derivatives?
Did historical AAP discipline analyses intentionally include vehicle Incident rows, and what current AAP methodology defines the disciplinary reporting population?
automation_candidates: Generate AAP views from one authoritative event register rather than maintaining manual sorted copies.
Create deterministic reconciliation tests that fail if source/derivative event populations differ without an approved transformation note.
Recalculate subgroup totals from detail records and compare with historical hard-coded subtotal rows.
Version EEO/job-group mapping tables by plan year so recoding is explicit and reproducible.

provenance.page_or_section: AAP derivative integrity comparison / formula scan
provenance.notes: Comparisons performed locally against restricted workbooks; only privacy-safe aggregate differences were promoted.
